title: One plain-click predicate for the kit's client-routed links
body:
## Summary
The 'plain left click, no modifier' rule is written three times in @gt/ui: Pile.tsx:51 (private), SlotRow.tsx:39 (exported plainClick), HeaderChips.tsx:24 (private).

## Description
Three links route a plain click client-side and leave modified clicks to the browser; each spells the predicate itself. A fourth button (middle-click, a new modifier) would have to be fixed three times. Fixed looks like one helper (e.g. packages/ui/src/components/link/plain.ts) imported by all three, with a unit case over the five fields. Pile alone could import SlotRow's plainClick, but that ties the Weir's pile to a calendar row's module and CSS for one predicate - so it was not built here.

## Flow
- grep -rn "!e.metaKey" packages app -> 3 sites
- build: move plainClick to a shared helper, import it at the 3 sites, one vitest case (button 1 / each modifier -> false; plain -> true)

## Expected impact
No user-visible change; one rule instead of three. Could break: a site that relied on its private type signature (React MouseEvent vs Pick).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one implementation of the plain-click rule
Before: 3 implementations (Pile.tsx:51, SlotRow.tsx:39, HeaderChips.tsx:24)
After: predicted 1
Method: simulation - two of the three sites are outside this context (floor-calendar-slots, header)
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: grep count of the predicate (3 -> 1) + a vitest case over the shared helper, seeded red by dropping one modifier

title: A ratified style's shelf tile draws its plate
body:
## Summary
ShelfStyle draws a bare gradient where the style's plate should sit, because the Floor's shelf row carries no plate.

## Description
packages/ui/src/components/floor/ShelfCell.tsx:59-62 draws `.hero.noHero` always; app/(studio)/floor/_floor/shelf.ts:29 ShelfStyleRow is {id, name, family}. The Library (Phase 5) serves style plates, so the data exists elsewhere in the tree. Fixed: the shelf read carries one kept plate url per proven style, and ShelfStyle takes an optional `plate` and draws it with an alt of the style's name (the empty ground stays for a style with none).

## Flow
- open the Floor -> Image lane -> Library · styles: every tile is the same gradient
- build: shelf.ts reads a plate per proven style (one kept forge plate / the style's first proof), ShelfStyle `plate?` prop, a floor.test.ts case for both arms

## Expected impact
The operator recognises a style by its look rather than its name. Could break: shelf read cost (one extra lookup per proven style; SHELF_ROWS caps at 24).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a ratified style is shown, not named only
Before: 0 of N proven-style tiles draw a plate
After: predicted N of N where a plate exists
Method: simulation - the data seam is app/(studio)/floor/_floor/shelf.ts, outside this context
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: floor.test.ts: ShelfStyle with plate renders , without plate keeps the ground; a next-server case that the shelf read returns a plate for a fixture style with kept plates

title: The Weir's arrival cascade waits 70 ms per pile, unbounded
body:
## Summary
Pile's animation delay is index x 70 ms with no cap, so the Nth pile in a lane is invisible for 70N + 700 ms after the Floor mounts.

## Description
packages/ui/src/components/floor/Pile.tsx:66 sets --d to `${index * 70}ms`; Pile.module.css:3 runs pileIn .7s with `both` fill, so the pile is at opacity 0 until its delay ends. At 12 piles the last appears at 1.54 s; at 30, 2.8 s. Fixed: cap the stagger (e.g. min(index, 8)) so the cascade reads as arrival without hiding work.

## Flow
- open the Floor with a lane holding many piles -> the last piles fade in seconds after the first
- build: cap index in the delay; measure the last pile's visible-at on the fixture side and on a store with many piles

## Expected impact
The operator sees every waiting pile within ~1.3 s. Could break: nothing functional; the cascade shape changes past the cap.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - time until every waiting pile is visible
Before: 70N + 700 ms (unbounded in N)
After: predicted <= 70 x cap + 700 ms
Method: simulation - no pile-count distribution read from the fixture or a real store this round
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: count piles per lane on the fixture side and the operator-shaped store (temp copy); the max-delay figure before/after the cap
